SEO Tip: Here's a great search operator to mine Reddit for key questions. Perform a Reddit "site:" search for a topic + "intitle:?" to find questions:  

Author's Note: As always everyone, to get my top LinkedIn posts right to your inbox, check out the newsletter in my bio.  

So this was a nice tip I saw from [**Surfer SEO Expert**](https://www.linkedin.com/company/surfer-seo-expert/)'s YouTube channel the other day. They created pretty nice search operator to mine Reddit for different questions:  

1. Perform a site search on Reddit (site:reddit(dot)com)  
2. Choose the topic you want to analyze threads for. This could be key topical area, your brand or something else  
3. Leverage intitle:? to ensure that only threads with dedicated questions come up  

You'll then see a list of Reddit threads that are specifically question based. You get a bit more insights into what questions users specifically have around your products or topical areas.

If anyone wants this at volume, Reddit will hand it over as data instead. Any listing or search URL answers with JSON if you put .json on the end, so you can pull the titles and do the question-mark filter yourself. The catch is the public endpoint rate limits hard when you are not authenticated, so past a few hundred rows it needs a token and a sleep between pages.
